    Tidy, glance and augment meta-analytic fits

    Source: R/broom-methods.R
    meta_fit_tidiers.Rd

    broom style tidiers for <meta_fit> objects. tidy() returns the coefficient table, glance() a one row summary of heterogeneity and fit statistics, and augment() the study level data with fitted values, residuals and diagnostics.

    Usage

    # S3 method for class 'meta_fit'
tidy(x, exponentiate = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'meta_fit'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'meta_fit'
augment(x, data = NULL, ...)

    Arguments

    x

    A <meta_fit>.

    exponentiate

    Exponentiate the estimates and confidence limits? Useful for log risk, odds and rate ratios.

    ...

    Not used.

    data

    Optional data to augment. Defaults to the data used in the fit (with the filled studies for meta_trimfill()).

    Value

    tidy() and augment() return tibbles. glance() returns a one row tibble with nobs, method, test, tau2, its Q-profile confidence limits (tau2.low, tau2.high), tau, I2, H2, R2, QE, df.residual, p.QE, QM, p.QM, the prediction interval (pred.low, pred.high), logLik, AIC and BIC, plus model specific columns (subgroup tests, variance components or the number of filled studies). augment() adds .study, .yi, .vi, .fitted, .resid, .std_resid, .hat, .weight (in percent) and .blup (the empirical Bayes estimate of each study's true effect).

    Examples

    bcg <- meta_effect_size(bcg_trials, "RR",
  event1 = tpos, n1 = tpos + tneg, event2 = cpos, n2 = cpos + cneg
)
fit <- meta_pool(bcg)
tidy(fit, exponentiate = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   term    estimate std.error statistic   p.value conf.low conf.high
#>   <chr>      <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 overall    0.489     0.180     -3.97 0.0000705    0.344     0.696
glance(fit)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 21
#>   model_type  nobs method test   tau2 tau2.low tau2.high   tau    I2    H2    R2
#>   <chr>      <int> <chr>  <chr> <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 pool          13 REML   z     0.313    0.120      1.11 0.560  92.2  12.9    NA
#> # ℹ 10 more variables: QE <dbl>, df.residual <int>, p.QE <dbl>, QM <dbl>,
#> #   p.QM <dbl>, pred.low <dbl>, pred.high <dbl>, logLik <dbl>, AIC <dbl>,
#> #   BIC <dbl>
augment(fit)
